A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while the C4 pathway is an evolutionary adaptation for photosynthesis at elevated O2 concentrations, the evolution of the C4 pathway was not a simple process.
C4 photosynthesis evolved from an intermediate state in which CO2 was concentrated in the bundle sheath cells and the C4 cycle was not fully developed.

C3-C4 intermediates are plants with a low C4 cycle capacity that is sufficient only to maintain the C4 cycle at a low CO2 compensation concentration, but that does not permit the C4 cycle to operate at a low CO, compensation concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C4 pathway evolved in a stepwise manner from the C3 pathway, with each step conferring a benefit to the plant.
the C4 photosynthesis is a result of a long evolutionary process, which started with the appearance of the first C3-C4 intermediates.
the evolution of C3-C4 intermediates to C4 species was not a simple process, but rather a gradual transition that involved several steps.
